about: THROUGH THE DOOR: Open Graph card specs for 14 artbitrage.io rooms (tools/brand/gen_card.py). Glyphs come from map.json (cjk) unless glyph_source says otherwise. Walls, inks and accents come from each room's own CSS tokens. Mounts copy the room's own CSS mount (mount_source). Title, maker and date come from the museum record named in record_source; title uses the record's display_title where it has one. accent_word is the word the room's h1 sets in italic. image is empty for rooms with no key work, which get a typographic card. Paths are relative to the repo root. card_alt is the og:image:alt text the page carries for its card.

rooms.title: Saint George and the Dragon
rooms.record_source: explore.html readings-data (title, artist, date). Licence checked at the source: the AIC API record https://api.artic.edu/api/v1/artworks/15468 gives is_public_domain true and copyright_notice null (2026-10-09T19:37:56Z); catalog/all.json id 15468 also labels it CC0 (source-declared). The image is the legacy /art/ mirror, which has no credits.json; its sha256 and size are recorded here, but no download receipt exists for it.

rooms.title: Cupid and Psyche
rooms.record_source: catalog/psyche.json (title, artist, date, museum URL; rights source-declared CC0, credit 'Gift of Isidor Straus, 1905'). The room has no credits.json, so the licence was checked at the source: the Met API record https://collectionapi.metmuseum.org/public/collection/v1/objects/188954 gives isPublicDomain true and an empty rightsAndReproduction, recorded here as copyright_notice null (2026-10-09T21:20:11Z). The image is the Met's own primaryImage https://images.metmuseum.org/CRDImages/es/original/DP248228.jpg: fetched again on 2026-10-09 it is byte-identical to assets/psyche/canova.jpg (sha256 and size below, as catalog/psyche.json records).
rooms.mount_source: psyche.html .image-frame: border 1px solid #272320; .work-first .image-frame: background #19191a, padding 0 (the room's first work hangs edge to edge inside a hairline frame, so the card draws the hairline and no mat)
rooms.card_alt: Artbitrage card: “The Lamp Between Us”, beneath 共照 and “A room after Cupid & Psyche”. Through an arched doorway in a near-black wall, the Met’s photograph of Antonio Canova’s plaster Cupid and Psyche, the winged Cupid bending over Psyche, hangs in a hairline frame in the next room.
